title: Audit a fractional row-basis certificate on residual P104 tight cubes
body:
The tested 24-port row mixtures have exact score ceilings 43 and 339/8 for i3 and i5. Both fall below the budget-55 contradiction threshold. The inherited 665/1,001 cube exclusions are reproduced.

## Scope and source

Uses the #7893 residual cube audit and the named 12- and 24-port families. The bound concerns those fractional certificate families. DreamingOfClouds’ Q=0 and thin toolkit extension is #7869 at `06c207a9feb3994a4b987dc3010657b6e85b7956`. The archive identifies additional inputs by exact commit, path and hash. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; P104 toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-blinear-fractional-row-bases/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory. Check its inner checksum manifest. The clean standard-library replay rebuilt both source cubes, all four exact score ceilings and eleven corruption controls. The extracted README gives the complete command. The archive preserves the verification evidence and controls. This is an offline research archive; hosted package execution is separate.

## Open next questions

Try other port selections or proof-producing branch checks on the 336 residual cube IDs. The two full cubes remain undecided by this method.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. Related results: [P104 campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
